paras: The beating of William Green by Shreveport police took place in Shreveport, Louisiana, in mid-June 1881, when Policeman Wimbish struck Green, a Black man wanted for larceny, several times over the head with his pistol during his arrest. A crowd of Black residents gathered and threatened to free Green, and the police chief ordered the arrest of its leaders. The only account is a Shreveport Times item, reprinted twice in a Baton Rouge paper, that tells the story from the officer's side.
According to the Shreveport Times, the police had been looking for Green, printed as "Willian Green," for several weeks on a charge of larceny.

Between 6 and 7 o'clock one evening, Wimbish found Green in a store near the ferry landing. Green ran toward Jones' saw mill and was outpacing the officer when Wiley Downs came out of the mill, caught him, and held him until Wimbish arrived. In the Times account, Green then seized Wimbish by the throat and swore "that there were not policemen enough in town to arrest him." Wimbish drew his pistol and struck Green "several blows over the head" until he let go, and Downs and another man helped secure him.

Meanwhile "a large number of negroes" assembled, "violently opposed" Wimbish and Downs, and threatened to rescue Green. The paper credited "the coolness and determination displayed by the white men" with preventing the rescue.

That night Chief Austin instructed the force to arrest the ringleaders of the crowd and lock them up. The coverage does not report the extent of Green's injuries, the outcome of the larceny charge, or whether any members of the crowd were arrested.

The story survives through the Louisiana Capitolian of Baton Rouge, which reprinted the Shreveport Times item in its state news column on June 21, 1881, and ran the same column again on June 25. The Times wrote from the officers' side, describing Green as a man "of superior physical strength" and "the desperate negro," and gave no account from Green or from the people who gathered; the Capitolian added no comment.

reader.title: Beating of William Green by Shreveport police
bases: A Shreveport policeman beat Green over the head with his pistol while arresting him for larceny; no mob attacked Green, and the crowd that gathered was Black residents opposing the arrest (A2).
The only account is one Shreveport Times item, carried by the Louisiana Capitolian on June 21 and again on June 25 (A2, A3); no independent report was found.

accounts.label: Shreveport Times (officer's side)
accounts.gist: Green fled, was caught by Downs, then seized Wimbish by the throat and swore no police could arrest him; Wimbish struck him with his pistol until he let go, and a Black crowd threatened a rescue.

framing.detail: The Times presented the beating as a response to Green's choking of the officer, called him 'the desperate negro' of 'superior physical strength', and praised 'the white men' for stopping a rescue.
The Baton Rouge Louisiana Capitolian carried the Times item without comment in its state news column, twice.

info: Between 6 and 7 o'clock on the evening before the Shreveport Times item; the Times date is not given, so the event fell on or before about June 20, 1881.
Near the ferry landing and Jones' saw mill, Shreveport.
William Green (printed 'Willian Green'), described as 'a negro man'.
Wanted by police for several weeks on a charge of larceny.
Policeman Wimbish struck Green; Wiley Downs and another unnamed man helped hold him.

sources.note: State news column reprinting the Shreveport Times: Wimbish arrests Green for larceny, beats him with his pistol; Black crowd threatens rescue; Chief Austin orders ringleaders arrested.
quotes: For several weeks the police have been on the alert for a negro man named Willian Green, who is wanted for larceny.
Mr. Wimbish managed to get his pistol out and dealt the negro several blows over the head before he could be induced to relax his hold.
Meantime a large number of negroes had assembled and violently opposed the officer and Mr. Downs and threatened to rescue Green at all hazards
Last night Chief Austin instructed the force to arrest the ring leaders and lock them up.
